newsitem.title: MONACO: RALLYING-MAKINEN IN LEAD IN MONTE CARLO.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-MAKINEN IN LEAD IN MONTE CARLO.

text.p: Leading overall placings in
the Monte Carlo world championship rally after nine timed stages
on Tuesday:
1. Tommi Makinen (Finland) Mitsubishi Lancer 2 hours 28
minutes 19 seconds
2. Carlos Sainz (Spain) Ford Escort 2:28:23
3. Piero Liatti (Italy) Subaru Impreza 2:28:34
4. Armin Schwarz (Germany) Ford Escort 2:31:12
5. Didier Auriol (France) Ford Escort 2:32:27
6. Dieter Depping (Germany) Ford Escort 2:35:12
7. Uwe Nittel (Germany) Mitsubishi Lancer 2:35:28
8. Olivier Burri (Switzerland) Subaru Impreza 2:39:37
9. Henrik Lundgaard (Denmark) Toyota Celica 2:40:13
10. Gustavo Trelles (Spain) Mitsubishi Lancer 2:41:32
MONTE CARLO, Jan 21 (Reuter) - Briton Colin McRae retired
from the Monte Carlo rally after Tuesday's icy first test in the
Vercors mountains which allowed Finn Tommi Makinen to seize the
race lead.
McRae, who had dropped to fourth place overall after hitting
a snowdrift on Monday, went off the road again in the third
day's opening timed stage over 33 kms from St Jean en Royans to
La Chapelle en Vercors.
The 1995 world champion broke the rear left suspension and
damaged the steering of his new Subaru Impreza, his team said.
He managed to finish the stage despite a badly damaged rear left
wheel but ended it over 24 minutes behind his Subaru team mate
Piero Liatti of Italy, who clocked the best time.
As no technical assistance was allowed before the start of
the next section, McRae had to pull out, his team added.
The second fastest time 13 seconds slower than Liatti was
enough to give reigning world champion Makinen first place in
the overall placings in his Mitsubishi Lancer.
Overnight leader Carlos Sainz of Spain, who had started the
day three seconds ahead of Makinen, could only manage the third
fastest time and lost 18 seconds on his rival.
With five timed stages remaining on the penultimate day of
the winter classic, Makinen was in the lead with Liatti in
second place eight seconds behind and Sainz third a further
seven seconds back.
